assays.assay_description: Rats placed in clear acrylic cylinder (height 40 cm, diameter 20.3 cm) filled with water (23 ± 1 °C). Preswim 15 min on day 0; 5-min test swim 24 h after dosing and again 7 days post-injection. Immobility, climbing, and swimming behaviors scored via 5-s time sampling by blinded technicians.

application_type.evidence: Rats were given intraperitoneal injections of either saline, ketamine (10 mg/kg), or zalsupindole (10 mg/kg)

setup_habituation.evidence: The first swim session (preswim) lasted for 15 min

setup_restrain.evidence: Only one rat was placed in the swim chamber at a time

food_restriction.evidence: Food and water provided ad libitum in home cage; no food in FST chamber during the 5-min test

water_restriction.evidence: No drinking water available in the swim chamber during the test

time_to_assay.evidence: Rats were given intraperitoneal injections... ~24 h prior to the FST. Same rats were retested on day 7 post injection.

sample_size.evidence: Male Sprague-Dawley rats... (N = 10 per treatment group)

outcomes.summary: A single IP dose of zalsupindole (10 mg/kg) produced a rapid (24 h) decrease in immobility in the FST that was sustained at 7 days, comparable to ketamine (10 mg/kg).
outcomes.statistics: one-way ANOVA with Dunnett's post hoc test; * P < 0.05, ** P < 0.01, *** P < 0.001, **** P < 0.0001 as compared to the VEH control
outcomes.evidence: ZAL produced a rapid (within 24 h) decrease in immobility (Figure 5B) that was sustained for at least a week (Figure 5C).

B1_num_measures.evidence: The measures were immobility, climbing, and swimming behaviors.

B2_temporal_dynamics.evidence: Time-sampled scoring over the 5-min session; no within-session temporal binning reported.

B3_sequential_structure.evidence: No transition or sequence analysis reported.

B4_ethological.evidence: FST immobility/swim/climb are stress-coping measures, not natural ethological behaviours.

B5_social.evidence: Only one rat was placed in the swim chamber at a time.

B7_automated_classification.evidence: Scoring of the swim test was performed by trained technicians using a time sampling technique.

B8_multivariate.evidence: No PCA or multivariate analysis reported.

E1_environment_type.evidence: Each FST chamber was constructed of clear acrylic (height = 40 cm; diameter = 20.3 cm).

E7_social_context.evidence: Only one rat was placed in the swim chamber at a time.

E8_food_water.evidence: No food or drinking water accessible during the test.

D1_continuity.evidence: All rats were exposed to two swim sessions... Same rats were retested on day 7 post injection.

D2_session_duration.evidence: the second swim session... lasted for 5 min

D3_recording_days.evidence: Test 24 h after dosing and again on day 7 post injection.

D4_baseline.evidence: Preswim was 15 min before dosing but its data is not reported as a scored outcome (used for habituation).

D5_followup.evidence: Same rats were retested on day 7 post injection.

assays.assay_description: C57BL/6J male mice habituated to test cage for 30 min, then injected IP with psilocybin (1 mg/kg), DOI (1 mg/kg), or zalsupindole (10 or 30 mg/kg) and placed back in cage. HTR (rapid side-to-side head shaking) scored in real time by blinded observers over a 20-min observation period.

application_type.evidence: receive psilocybin (1 mg/kg, IP), DOI (1 mg/kg, IP), zalsupindole (10 mg/kg, IP), or zalsupindole (30 mg/kg, IP)

setup_habituation.evidence: The C57BL/6J male mice were habituated to the test cage for at least 30 min prior to the test.

setup_restrain.evidence: the mice were placed back in the test cage for a 20 min observation period

food_restriction.evidence: Standard short HTR test; no food provided in test cage during recording.

water_restriction.evidence: Standard short HTR test; no water in test cage during recording.

time_to_assay.evidence: Test compounds were injected immediately prior to testing. Directly post-treatment, the mice were placed back in the test cage for a 20 min observation period.

sample_size.evidence: Young adult C57BL/6J male mice (5-6 weeks old at arrival; N = 70)

outcomes.summary: Psilocybin (1 mg/kg) and DOI (1 mg/kg) induced robust head-twitch responses, whereas zalsupindole (10 or 30 mg/kg) did not induce HTR, consistent with its proposed nonhallucinogenic profile.
outcomes.evidence: ZAL does not induce a mouse head-twitch response (HTR).

B1_num_measures.evidence: The HTR activity was defined as rapid side to side head shaking

B2_temporal_dynamics.evidence: Total HTRs over 20 min reported; no within-session time-course analysis.

B4_ethological.evidence: Head-twitch response is explicitly listed as NOT ethological in the rubric.

B7_automated_classification.evidence: scored by experienced, blinded testers in real time

E2_shelter.evidence: No enclosed refuge mentioned in test cage.

E3_bedding.evidence: Not described as present in test cage.

E7_social_context.evidence: Mice tested individually in the test cage.

E8_food_water.evidence: No food/water in test cage during recording.

judge_notes: Included two behavioural assays: Forced Swim Test (rats) and Head-Twitch Response (mice). Dropped electrophysiology (sEPSCs), Golgi-Cox dendritic spine analysis, microdialysis, pharmacokinetics, radioligand binding, and in vitro neurite outgrowth assays as non-behavioural.
Species reported as 'mouse and rat' since FST used rats and HTR used mice; strain captures both.

HTR outcome direction set to 'no_effect' for the psychedelic of primary interest (zalsupindole), while noting psilocybin/DOI positive controls did induce HTR; this matches the rubric's framing of direction for ZAL.
Added Ketamine to dosing list (active comparator) and included DMT (used in sEPSC dosing) even though DMT was not used in a scored behavioural assay, to preserve compound metadata.
Preswim in FST treated as habituation, not a scored baseline (D4=0), since preswim data is not reported as an analysed outcome.
